mainTopic: אסמכתא: when conditional promises to pay with land or goods take effect, and what follows when they don't
overview: This amud keeps asking when an אסמכתא works. An אסמכתא is a conditional promise like 'if I don't pay, take my field,' which a person makes without really expecting to keep it. First the גמרא says the משנה's lender gets the field if the borrower said 'acquire from now.' Then רב אשי tries to read a rule of רב נחמן as 'an offer before the due date works, after it does not,' but the גמרא rejects this: even before the due date, the borrower was only buying quiet. Next comes a back-and-forth about signs that the borrower was not under pressure. The beer test and the price test are both knocked down, and the final test is whether he is attached to his land. רב פפא adds that a field can still be an אפותיקי, a set source of repayment, if the borrower said 'you will be paid only from this.' Two more cases follow: a seller's guarantee after a flood washed away his best land, and a promise to pay from wine, where רבה's rule teaches that any 'if' deal fails. Finally, רב נחמן rules that the land and its produce go back, and the גמרא explains why a loan is different from a sale when it comes to forgiving something by mistake.

steps.title: Another answer: he said 'acquire from now'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain why the משנה lets the lender get the field: the borrower said 'acquire it from now.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead that the borrower told the lender: 'If I don't pay by the deadline, acquire the field starting from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an extra answer to its earlier question of why the משנה's case is not a useless אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא fails because the borrower never fully meant to give the field. Saying 'from now' and making a קנין at that moment shows he truly meant to transfer it, so the deal stands once the condition is met.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say instead. This introduces an alternative answer.
Acquire from now. The transfer takes effect now, on condition.
A conditional promise made without full intent, which normally does not transfer ownership

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
that he said to him: 'Acquire from now.'
phrases.notes: The borrower is speaking to the lender, and 'it' is the field from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another answer to the earlier question about אסמכתא in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the borrower used 'from now' wording)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case looks like an ordinary אסמכתא, which should not transfer the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: The borrower said 'acquire from now,' which shows real intent, so the lender acquires the field.

steps.title: רב נחמן's rule: an אסמכתא acquires in its time
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רב חסדא tell רב אשי that the scholars of נהרדעא quote רב נחמן: an אסמכתא acquires 'in its time' but not 'not in its time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר ינוקא and מר קשישא, the sons of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי: The scholars of נהרדעא say in the name of רב נחמן that this kind of אסמכתא acquires at its proper time, but not when it is not its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought about when an אסמכתא works and when it doesn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says an אסמכתא can sometimes work, depending on 'its time.' It does not yet explain what 'its time' means. That unclear point is exactly what רב אשי will discuss next.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city נהרדעא
In the name of
In its time, at the proper time
It acquires, it takes effect as a קנין

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ מָר יָנוֹקָא וּמָר קַשִּׁישָׁא
phrases.english: Mar Yanuka and Mar Kashisha said to him,
the sons of Rav Chisda, to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמְרִי נְהַרְדְּעָאֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: This is what the scholars of Neharde'a say in the name of Rav Nachman:
This asmakhta acquires in its time,
not in its time, it does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמְרִי נְהַרְדְּעָאֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about when an אסמכתא works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אסמכתא acquires 'in its time' and does not acquire 'not in its time.'

steps.title: רב אשי: isn't that true of everything?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the rule as 'it only works on the due date' and objects that this is obvious for any transaction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to them: Every matter works that way. It acquires at its proper time and does not acquire when it is not its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the rule by asking what new thing it could be teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'in its time' just means the field passes to the lender once the deadline arrives, that is true of any conditional deal. So the plain reading leaves רב נחמן saying nothing new, and the statement needs a better explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Every matter, anything at all
He said to them

phrases.english: He said to them: Every matter,

phrases.aramaic: בְּזִמְנֵיהּ קָנֵי, בְּלָא זִמְנֵיהּ לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: in its time it acquires, not in its time it does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל מִידֵּי, בְּזִמְנֵיהּ קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement just quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule as reported by the sons of רב חסדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule, read simply, teaches nothing new. Every deal takes effect only at its proper time.

steps.title: רב אשי's reading: before the due date versus after it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests a new meaning. If the borrower offered the field before the deadline, the lender acquires it. If he offered it after the deadline, the lender does not, because the borrower only said it out of shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is what you mean. If the borrower met the lender before the due date and told him, 'Acquire the field,' he acquires it. If it was after the due date and he told him, 'Acquire,' he does not acquire it. Why not? Because the borrower only said it out of embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers his own challenge by giving רב נחמן's words a meaning that does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the due date there is no pressure yet, so an offer of the field is taken as sincere. After the due date, the borrower is ashamed that he can't pay and says 'take the field' only to save face. That is not real intent, so no קנין happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps this is what you are saying
Within its time, before the due date
After its time, once the due date has passed
Shame, embarrassment

steps.whatToRemember: In רב אשי's reading, an offer made before the due date counts as sincere, while one made after the due date comes from embarrassment and does not transfer the field. The next step rejects the first half of this.
steps.confusionAlert: 'In its time' here does NOT mean 'once the deadline arrives.' רב אשי reads it as 'during the loan period, before the deadline.' Offers made after the deadline are the ones that fail.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what you are saying:
If he met him within its time
and said to him 'Acquire,' he acquires;

phrases.aramaic: בָּתַר זִמְנֵיהּ וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ קְנִי – לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: after its time, and he said to him 'Acquire,' he does not acquire.
What is the reason?
It is out of shame that he says it to him.
phrases.notes: The borrower is embarrassed that he can't pay, so his words don't reflect what he really wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא הָכִי קָאָמְרִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by reinterpreting 'in its time' from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In its time' means the field passes once the deadline arrives, which would be obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In its time' means the offer was made before the due date and is sincere. After the due date, it is said out of shame and does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether a קנין works depends on the person's real intent. Words said under social pressure or embarrassment are not treated as a true decision to transfer property.

steps.title: Even before the deadline, the lender does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's distinction. Even if the borrower offered the field before the deadline, the lender does not acquire it, because the borrower only said it to avoid being bothered later.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Even if he said it before the due date, the lender does not acquire. Why did the borrower say 'acquire'? He thought: this way, when the due date comes, the lender will not come and bother me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's explanation from the previous step and says the lender never acquires, not even before the deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said an offer made before the deadline was sincere. The גמרא says it is not. The borrower was only buying peace and quiet so the lender would leave him alone, so the offer is still an empty אסמכתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the גמרא rejects the previous idea
Within its time, meaning before the due date
Acquire! (the borrower's words to the lender)
He will disturb me, or bother me

phrases.english: But it is not so,
for even within its time
phrases.notes: Even if the borrower made the offer before the due date, which is the case רב אשי said works.

phrases.english: he also does not acquire,
and the fact that he said to him "acquire":
he thinks:
when the due date arrives,
he will not come and bother me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's distinction between before and after the deadline
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's claim that an offer made before the deadline transfers the field
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An offer made before the deadline is also not sincere. The borrower only wanted to avoid being pressured when the due date came.

steps.title: Sometimes an אסמכתא works and sometimes it does not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says it depends on the borrower's state. If the lender found him relaxed, drinking beer, the lender acquires. If he found him anxiously hunting for money, the lender does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this אסמכתא sometimes acquires and sometimes does not. If the lender found the borrower drinking beer, it acquires. If he found him searching for coins, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new rule: whether the אסמכתא works depends on what the borrower seemed like at the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower who is calmly drinking is not under pressure, so his promise seems serious. A borrower scrambling for money is desperate, so his promise is just words said under stress.

keyTerms.meaning: A conditional promise the person does not really expect to have to keep
Sometimes
Drinking beer
Searching for money (literally, turning over coins)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
this asmakhta,
sometimes it acquires and sometimes it does not acquire.
If he found him drinking beer, he acquires.
If he was searching for money, he does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי אַסְמַכְתָּא, זִימְנִין קָנְיָא וְזִימְנִין לָא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the timing distinction, offers a different test based on the borrower's state of mind
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אסמכתא works if the borrower seemed relaxed (drinking beer) and fails if he seemed desperate (hunting for money).

steps.title: Drinking beer does not prove he was relaxed
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי argues that the beer test proves nothing. Maybe he drank to calm his fear. Or maybe someone else promised him money, so he is still not secure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: Maybe he was drinking to calm his fear. Or maybe another person promised him money, and he is relying on that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי attacks רב פפא's beer test and says it is not a reliable sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking might be a way to drown worry, not a sign of calm. Even if he has money lined up, it depends on someone else's promise, so he may still be under pressure. Either way, the promise could still be an empty אסמכתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
To ease, or calm, his fear
Alternatively
Promised him, so he is relying on it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina:
perhaps he was drinking to calm his fear,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: אִינִישׁ אַחֲרִינָא אַסְמְכֵיהּ אַזּוּזֵי!
phrases.english: or else, another person promised him money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: דִּלְמָא לְפַכּוֹחֵי פַּחְדֵּיהּ קָא שָׁתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sign רב פפא used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drinking beer does not prove the borrower is free of pressure. It could come from fear, or from relying on someone else's uncertain promise.

steps.title: New sign: he is fussy about the price
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a different sign. If the borrower insists on getting full value for his property, the lender certainly acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: if he is particular about the price, the lender certainly acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא drops the beer test and replaces it with a new sign: whether the borrower is fussy about getting a fair price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone desperate for money will sell cheap. A borrower who refuses to sell below market value is clearly not desperate, so his promise to give the field was made seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the earlier idea is dropped and a new one is offered
Particular, fussy, insistent
About the money or price
He certainly acquires

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:
if he is particular about the price,
phrases.notes: He means the borrower won't sell his property for less than it's worth.

phrases.english: he certainly acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא: אִי קָפֵיד בִּדְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing the beer test with a better sign
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the challenged criterion with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Drinking beer shows the borrower is relaxed
steps.terutzMaskana: Insisting on full price shows the borrower is not under financial pressure

steps.title: Being fussy about price may just protect his land values
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי objects again. The borrower may act fussy about price only so the value of his lands won't drop, even though he is really under pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: Maybe he thinks he should act this way so that his land will not become cheap.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי challenges רבינא's new sign and says it is also unreliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people knew he was desperate, buyers would push his prices down. So he might demand full price just to keep up appearances, while he is actually still under stress.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will not
Become cheap, drop in value
His land

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina:
perhaps he thinks
so that his land will not become cheap,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: דִּלְמָא סָבַר כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תִּיתְּזִיל אַרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's replacement sign
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Insisting on a high price could be a strategy to protect the market value of his property, not proof that he is free of pressure.

steps.title: Final sign: he is fussy about keeping his land
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives the final test. If the borrower is attached to his land and doesn't want to sell it at all, the lender certainly acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: if he is particular about the land, the lender certainly acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on a final sign: whether the borrower is attached to the land itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being fussy about price could be a pose. But a borrower who doesn't want to part with his land even at full value is clearly not desperate for cash. So his promise was serious and the אסמכתא works.

keyTerms.meaning: About the land itself
If he is particular about keeping the land

steps.whatToRemember: An אסמכתא normally does not transfer ownership, because the promise was not meant seriously. But if the borrower clearly is not under pressure, shown by his not wanting to give up his land at all, the lender acquires.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'fussy' tests. רבינא's test is about the price, which could be a pose. רב פפא's final test is about the land itself, which shows real lack of pressure.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
if he is particular about the land,
phrases.notes: He means the borrower doesn't want to sell his land at all, not even for its full price.

phrases.english: he certainly acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי קָפֵיד בְּאַרְעָא, וַדַּאי קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the last challenge with a sign that cannot be explained as a pose
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the challenged criterion with a stronger one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being fussy about price proves he is not under pressure
steps.terutzMaskana: Only real attachment to the land proves he is not under pressure, and then the lender acquires
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The test for a valid אסמכתא is whether the borrower is attached to his land. If he is, he was not desperate, and the lender acquires.

steps.title: רב פפא: the field still works as a designated repayment
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that even though an אסמכתא does not transfer ownership, the promised field becomes an אפותיקי that the lender can collect from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The Sages ruled that an אסמכתא does not transfer ownership. Even so, the field is set aside as an אפותיקי, so the lender can collect his debt from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a new ruling. The lender does not own the field outright, but the field is still set aside as the place he can collect his debt from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the question was whether the lender owns the field. רב פפא says the lender does not own it, because it is an אסמכתא. He then adds a middle option: the field becomes an אפותיקי, so the lender collects from it only up to the amount of the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: A conditional promise the person did not really expect to carry out, so it does not take legal effect
Does not acquire; does not transfer ownership
A designated field set aside as the source of repayment for a debt
To collect from it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ideas. An אסמכתא means the lender does NOT own the field. An אפותיקי means he can still collect his debt from it, but only up to the amount owed, not the whole field as a bonus.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows: can a failed אסמכתא still leave behind a lien on the field?

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
Even though the Sages said
an asmakhta does not effect acquisition,
it is a designated repayment, to collect from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אַסְמַכְתָּא לָא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling when the lender acquires the field, רב פפא addresses what happens when it is an אסמכתא and the lender does not acquire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the stipulation is an אסמכתא and does not transfer ownership, the field is an אפותיקי from which the lender may collect his debt.

steps.title: Did the borrower ever say the field was for collecting the debt?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא: the borrower never said 'acquire it to collect your debt,' so why should the field be an אפותיקי?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא: Did the borrower tell the lender, 'Acquire the field to collect your debt'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא's ruling. The borrower's words never set the field aside for collecting the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower promised to give the field as a full transfer, almost like a penalty, not as payment of the loan. Once that promise fails because it is an אסמכתא, nothing in his words is left to create an אפותיקי.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he say to him? (a challenging question)
Acquire!
Debt collection

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, said to Rav Pappa:
Did he say to him:
Acquire it for debt collection?
phrases.notes: He means no. The borrower only said 'take the field,' never 'take it as payment for the loan.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא: מִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ קְנִי לְגוּבְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב פפא's ruling in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the field becomes an אפותיקי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The borrower's words gave the field as an outright transfer, not as a source for collecting the debt. Once the transfer fails, nothing in his words creates a lien.

steps.title: Even saying 'for collection' would still be an אסמכתא
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי pushes the challenge further: even if the borrower had said 'acquire it for collection,' it would still be an אסמכתא and would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי said to רבינא: And if the borrower had said, 'Acquire it to collect from it,' would the lender acquire? In the end it is still an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not transfer ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא makes the problem with רב פפא's ruling even bigger. Different wording would not help, because the whole promise depends on a condition, so it is an אסמכתא either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's challenge suggested that the right words ('for collection') might create an אפותיקי. מר זוטרא says no: as long as the promise depends on 'if I don't pay,' it remains an אסמכתא. This leaves us asking what רב פפא could have meant.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he had said
Does he acquire?
In the end; after all is said

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמַר קְנִי לְמִיגְבֵּא מִינֵּיהּ – קָנֵי?
phrases.english: And if he had said, 'Acquire it to collect from it,' would he acquire?
In the end, it is an asmakhta,
and an asmakhta does not effect acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא: וְאִי אָמַר קְנִי לְמִיגְבֵּא מִינֵּיהּ קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב הונא's wording-based challenge and widens it: the wording makes no difference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea suggested by step 12 that saying 'for collection' could make the field an אפותיקי, and with it רב פפא's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any promise that depends on the borrower failing to pay is an אסמכתא, whatever the wording, so it cannot create a lien on the field either.

steps.title: So what kind of designated repayment did רב פפא mean?
steps.stepSummary: Since the earlier challenges seem to rule out any אפותיקי here, the גמרא asks what case רב פפא was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the אפותיקי that רב פפא spoke about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenges and asks what case רב פפא had in mind. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenges showed that a conditional 'if I don't pay, take it' cannot create an אפותיקי. So רב פפא must have meant a different kind of statement, and the גמרא wants to identify it.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather; if so (here it opens a rethinking)
What is it?

phrases.english: But the designated repayment that Rav Pappa spoke of,
what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַפּוֹתֵיקֵי דְּאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenges of steps 12-13 and asks how to understand רב פפא's statement in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case does רב פפא's אפותיקי refer to, given that a conditional promise cannot create one?

steps.title: A field named as the only source of payment
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא meant a borrower who said, 'You will be repaid only from this field,' which is a plain lien and not an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the borrower said to the lender: 'You will have no repayment except from this field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב פפא was talking about a borrower who clearly named one field as the only place he would pay from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'you will be paid only from this' does not depend on a condition like 'if I fail to pay.' It is a direct, serious commitment, so it is not an אסמכתא. That commitment is what makes the field an אפותיקי.

keyTerms.meaning: You will not have
Repayment
From this one (this field)

steps.whatToRemember: An אסמכתא ('if I don't pay, take the field') does not transfer the field. But if the borrower says 'you will be repaid only from this field,' the field becomes an אפותיקי, a real designated source of repayment.

phrases.english: Where he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא לְךָ פֵּרָעוֹן אֶלָּא מִזּוֹ.
phrases.english: You will have repayment only from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לֹא יְהֵא לְךָ פֵּרָעוֹן אֶלָּא מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and saves רב פפא's ruling from the challenges.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא's אפותיקי is a case where the borrower said, 'You will have repayment only from this field,' a direct lien that is not conditional and so not an אסמכתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A conditional transfer is an אסמכתא and fails, but an explicit statement that the debt will be paid only from a certain field creates a valid אפותיקי.

steps.title: A seller refuses to guarantee from his very best land
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a man sold land with a guarantee. The buyer asked to be repaid from the seller's very best land if the field was taken away, and the seller refused, offering other good land instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man sold land to another man with a guarantee. The buyer said: 'If the field is taken away from me, will you let me collect from your very best land?' The seller said: 'I won't let you collect from my very best land, because I want to keep it for myself. But I will let you collect from other good land that I have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a sale with a guarantee. This step sets out the agreement between buyer and seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With אחריות, if the seller's creditors take the field from the buyer, the seller must pay the buyer back. Here the two sides argued over which land the buyer could collect from: the seller kept his very best land off-limits and promised other good-quality land.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee: the seller will repay the buyer if the land is taken away
They seize (creditors taking land away)
The very best of the best-quality land
Best-quality land
To keep for myself (literally, to stand before me)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold land
to another with a guarantee.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי טָרְפוּ לַיהּ מִנַּאי
phrases.english: He said to him: If they seize it from me,
phrases.notes: The buyer is speaking. 'They' are the seller's creditors, who might come and take the field.

phrases.aramaic: מַגְבֵּית לִי מֵעִידֵּי עִידִּית דְּאִית לָךְ.
phrases.english: will you let me collect from the very best of the best land that you have?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵעִידֵּי עִידִּית לָא מַגְבֵּינָא לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: I will not let you collect from the very best of the best land,
because I want to keep it for myself,
but I will let you collect
from other best-quality land that I have.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, so read it as אחריתי, 'other.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ אַרְעָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ בְּאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case, unrelated in its details to רב פפא's אפותיקי, though it also deals with which land a person may collect from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet: this step lays out the agreement, in which the seller guaranteed the sale from good land but excluded his very best land.

steps.title: The field is taken and a flood ruins the best land
steps.stepSummary: In the end the buyer's field was taken away, and a flood swept away the seller's very best land.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, creditors took the field from the buyer, and a flood came and swept away the very best land.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point. The guarantee now has to be paid, but the land the seller wanted to keep has been ruined, which sets up the legal question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer is now owed payment under the guarantee. The very best land, which the seller had excluded, was destroyed by a flood. This raises a new question: does the buyer still collect from the 'other' good land, or does the flood change what that land now counts as?

keyTerms.meaning: In the end
A flood; a breach of water
Took; swept away

phrases.english: In the end, they seized it from him,
phrases.notes: Creditors took the field away from the buyer, so now the guarantee has to be paid.

phrases.english: and a flood came and swept away the very best of the best land.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף טַרְפוּהָ מִינֵּיהּ, אֲתָא בִּדְקָא שְׁקֵיל לְעִידֵּי עִידִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story of step 16 and sets up the coming legal question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet: the facts are now complete. The buyer's field was taken, and the seller's excluded very best land was destroyed by a flood.

steps.title: רב פפא's first thought: the buyer collects from the remaining good land
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא first thinks the seller must pay the buyer from his remaining עידית, since he promised good land and some good land still exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא thought to say: The seller promised to pay 'from superior land,' and look, superior land is still there, so he must pay from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his first idea about the flood case: the seller's promise is still in force, because good land is still available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very best land was washed away, but the seller still owns other עידית. רב פפא reads the promise as being about good land in general, so the seller must pay from what is left. The phrase סבר למימר warns us that this view will soon be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. A first idea that the גמרא usually goes on to reject.
Superior-quality land, the best category of fields.
It is standing, still in existence.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa thought to say:
He told him 'from superior land,'
and look, that is still standing.
phrases.notes: He means the seller still owns other good land, even though his very best field was washed away.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first ruling on the flood case set up in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial view: the seller must pay from his remaining עידית, since it still exists.

steps.title: The seller can say his remaining good land is now his 'very best'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי challenges this: the seller can argue that his remaining עידית now takes the place of the very best land he refused to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: But let the seller say: When I told you I would let you collect from good land, my very best land still existed. Now my good land has become my 'very best,' and I never agreed to give you my very best.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי argues against רב פפא's first idea by giving the seller a strong claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of the sale the seller refused to pay from his very best land and offered only his second-best. Now that the best is gone, the second-best has become his best. Making him give it would force him into exactly what he refused.

keyTerms.meaning: The very best of the superior land.
I will let you collect.
In place of.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels. עידי עידית was the very best, which the seller refused to give. עידית was the second-best he did offer. The flood turned the second-best into his new best.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha from Difti said to Ravina:
But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the seller, speaking to the buyer.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲמַרִי לָךְ אֲנָא מַגְבֵּינָא לָךְ –
phrases.english: When I told you, 'I will let you collect,'
that was when the very best land was still standing;
now the superior land stands for him
in place of the very best land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's first view in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's view that the seller must pay from his remaining עידית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller's refusal was about his best land. After the flood, his remaining עידית is now his best, so the refusal should protect it.
steps.whatToRemember: A promise is judged by what it meant when it was made. The seller refused to give his best, and the flood made his remaining good land his new best.

steps.title: A new case: 'If I don't pay by that day, collect from this wine'
steps.stepSummary: רב בר שבא owed money to רב כהנא and told him that if he didn't pay by a set date, רב כהנא could collect from a specific batch of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב בר שבא owed money to רב כהנא. He told him: If I don't pay you by such-and-such a day, collect from this wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story. It is setting up the next question: does this 'if' promise really work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise only takes effect 'if' he fails to pay on time. That shape of deal raises the question of אסמכתא, a promise a person makes while assuming he will never have to keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: He was owed money by him.
Such-and-such a day, a set date.
Collect.
Wine.

phrases.aramaic: רַב בַּר שְׁבָא הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: Rav bar Shabba owed Rav Kahana money.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי לָא פָּרַעְנָא לָךְ
phrases.english: He said to him: If I do not pay you
by such-and-such a day,
collect from this wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בַּר שְׁבָא הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the flood case ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case: a borrower promises that if he doesn't pay by a set date, the lender may collect from specific wine.

steps.title: רב פפא's first thought: wine is like money, so the promise works
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא first suggests that the rule 'אסמכתא does not acquire' applies only to land, while wine, which is made to be sold, counts like cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא thought to say: When we say an אסמכתא does not acquire, that is only for land, which is not meant to be sold. But wine is meant to be sold, so it is like money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא suggests a way for the wine promise to work despite the usual rule against אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person does not easily give up his land, so a conditional promise of land is assumed not to be serious. Wine is kept in order to be sold, so giving it up is like paying cash, and רב פפא thinks the promise is then real. Again, סבר למימר hints that this idea will be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A conditional promise a person makes assuming he will never have to keep it, so it is not taken as a real commitment.
Does not acquire, does not take legal effect.
Stands to be sold, meant for selling.
It is like money.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa thought to say:
When we say an asmachta does not acquire,
that applies only to land,
which is not meant to be sold.
But wine, since it is meant to be sold,
is like money.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא לְמֵימַר: כִּי אָמְרִינַן אַסְמַכְתָּא לָא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first ruling on the wine case from Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial view: the rule against אסמכתא applies to land, not to wine, which is treated like money.

steps.title: Any promise built on 'if' does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects רב פפא's distinction, quoting רבה: any deal that depends on 'if' is an אסמכתא and does not acquire, whether it is land or wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רב פפא: This is what we say in the name of רבה: Anything with 'if' does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע knocks down רב פפא's idea that wine is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with an אסמכתא is the shape of the promise, not the type of item. Once a deal says 'if this happens, you get that,' the person did not truly commit, so it fails for wine just as for land.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of רבה.
Anything with 'if,' any conditional deal.
Does not acquire.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the test for אסמכתא is the conditional 'if' wording. Whether the item is land or wine does not matter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a broad rule: conditional penalty-style promises generally do not take effect, no matter what is pledged.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
This is what we say in the name of Rabbah:
Anything with 'if' does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's distinction from Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that wine escapes the rule of אסמכתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אסמכתא depends on the conditional 'if' form of the promise, not on whether the item is usually sold.

steps.title: The land and the fruit must both go back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that since an אסמכתא does not acquire, the lender must return the land and also the fruit he ate from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Now that the חכמים have said that an אסמכתא does not acquire, the land goes back and the fruit goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן draws a practical result from the rule that an 'if' deal (אסמכתא) does not work: the lender who took the land must return it, along with what he ate from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower promised the land only if he failed to pay, so it was never really transferred. That means the lender ate fruit that was not his. Returning the land alone is not enough; he must also pay back the value of the fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: A promise made on an 'if' condition that the person never really expected to happen
Does not acquire, so ownership does not pass
The land goes back
Fruits or produce

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Now that the Sages have said
that an asmakhta does not acquire,
the land goes back and the fruit goes back.
phrases.notes: He means the value of the fruit the lender already ate has to be paid back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הַשְׁתָּא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אַסְמַכְתָּא לָא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion. Based on the general rule that an אסמכתא does not acquire, רב נחמן rules on returning the land and the produce in the משנה's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an אסמכתא fails, the lender returns both the land and the value of the produce he ate.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן think mistaken forgiveness is not forgiveness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן's ruling means he holds that forgiveness given by mistake does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רב נחמן holds that forgiving by mistake is not real forgiveness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an idea out of רב נחמן's ruling and checks it. This question is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower let the lender eat the fruit because he thought the land now belonged to the lender. That was a mistake. If the fruit must still be returned, it seems רב נחמן thinks permission given by mistake does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? The גמרא draws out an idea from a statement
Forgiveness or giving up a right, based on a mistake
Is not real forgiveness

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rav Naḥman holds
that mistaken forgiveness is not forgiveness?
phrases.notes: The borrower let the lender eat only because he wrongly thought the land was the lender's now.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pulls a broader principle out of רב נחמן's ruling in order to test it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב נחמן's ruling shows that he holds מחילה בטעות is not valid.

steps.title: רב נחמן's own ruling about palm fruit says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case of selling fruit before it grows, where רב נחמן admits the buyer who ate it keeps it, which shows that mistaken forgiveness does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If someone sells the fruit of a palm tree to his friend, רב הונא says: Before the fruit exists, the seller can back out. Once it exists, he cannot back out. רב נחמן says: Even once it exists, he can back out. And רב נחמן also said: I agree that if the buyer grabbed the fruit and ate it, we do not take it from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from the last step by quoting another ruling of רב נחמן that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the sale of fruit that did not yet exist never really worked, so the seller allowed the buyer to eat by mistake. Even so, רב נחמן says we do not take back what was eaten. That means he does treat mistaken forgiveness as real, which seems to contradict his ruling that the fruit from the land must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: A palm tree
Came into the world, meaning came into existence
To back out of the deal
Grabbed and ate
We do not take it away from him

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the sale works. He says the seller can back out. But if the buyer already ate the fruit, the seller cannot demand payment for it.

phrases.english: But it was stated:
One who sells the fruit of a palm tree to his fellow.
Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ לָעוֹלָם – יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Before they have come into the world, he can retract.

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לָעוֹלָם – אֵין יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Once they have come into the world, he cannot retract.
phrases.notes: Once the fruit exists, even if it is not ripe yet, the sale takes hold.

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לָעוֹלָם יָכוֹל לַחְזוֹר בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Even once they have come into the world, he can retract,
And Rav Naḥman said:
I concede that if he seized and ate,
we do not take it from him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיתְּמַר: הַמּוֹכֵר פֵּירוֹת דֶּקֶל לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses another ruling of רב נחמן to attack the idea raised in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב נחמן holds מחילה בטעות is not forgiveness, which is why the produce must be returned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the palm-fruit case the seller's permission was also a mistake, yet רב נחמן lets the buyer keep what he ate. So he must hold that mistaken forgiveness is valid, and then the lender should also keep the produce.

steps.title: A sale is different from a loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the palm case was a sale, while our case is a loan, where letting the lender keep the fruit would be a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it was a sale; here it is a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by pointing out that the two cases are different kinds of deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, we can say the seller truly gave up the fruit, and nothing is wrong with that. In a loan, if the lender keeps produce on top of being repaid, it is like taking extra for the loan, which is a form of רבית. So רב נחמן can hold that mistaken forgiveness counts and still require the produce to be returned here.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in the other case
A sale
A loan

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן does accept forgiveness given by mistake, as in a sale. But in a loan, the produce must still be returned, because keeping it would be like taking רבית.

phrases.english: There, it is a sale,
here, it is a loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם זְבִינֵי, הָכָא הַלְוָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve mistaken permission, so they should be judged the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a sale, mistaken forgiveness works. In a loan, keeping produce would be like taking רבית, so it must be returned.

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement of רבא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. The גמרא is setting up a new statement of רבא, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the speaker appears here. What רבא actually says follows right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said, which introduces his statement

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the sale-versus-loan answer.
